title: Haloumi Katsu Burgers
subtitle: with Carrot Salad and Spring Onion
description: Whether you're full-time vego or part-time only, our varied range of vegetarian dishes really hits the spot. Bursting with veggies, dairy, legumes, grains and nuts, they're packed with flavour, they’ll fill you up and they're totally mouth-watering too!

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Preheat the oven to 200C, fan-forced. Line an oven tray with baking paper. Peel the carrot into ribbons with a vegetable peeler. Halve the spring onion, then thinly slice lengthwise. Drain the haloumi and dry on paper towel, then cut in half horizontally to make 2 thin slices.

Crumb and roast haloumi: Put the haloumi on the lined tray, lightly brush all over with olive oil, then season with pepper. Put the breadcrumbs and 1 tsp olive oil in a bowl. Rub the oil into the breadcrumbs with your fingers until combined, then press onto the haloumi. Roast for 15 mins or until golden.

Make sauce and dressing: Meanwhile, put 2 tbs mayonnaise and 1 tsp soy sauce in a bowl and stir to combine (see Make it yours). Put 3 tsp soy sauce, 2 tsp olive oil, 1½ tsp white vinegar and 1½ tsp honey in a large bowl. Season with pepper and whisk to combine.

Grill bread rolls: Remove the haloumi from the oven and turn the oven to grill mode. Cut the bread rolls in half. Put on an oven tray, cut-side up, and grill for 1-2 mins until lightly toasted. Meanwhile, add the carrot and spinach to the dressing and gently toss to combine.

Serve up: Spread the rolls with the barbecue sauce. Layer the bases with some of the carrot salad and the haloumi. Drizzle with the mayo sauce, scatter with the spring onion, then sandwich with the tops. Serve with the remaining carrot salad and enjoy!
Make it yours: Add extra Japanese flair by stirring a little wasabi into the mayo sauce or add a squeeze of lemon juice for a citrusy twist.
